restrictions: Applies to the selected target poseidon-orchard-r@@R@@-prefix-v1 only (@@PARTIAL@@ plus the eight fixed full rounds); the construction uses the first two full rounds being skippable on a line and gives no claim for other round counts.

Algorithm paper, not executed: the program was not run at r = @@R@@. time_log2 is a worst-case operation count of the shipped source (at most K = @@K@@ centres, every trial charged in full, one thread), memory_log2_bytes its footprint. success_probability @@P_SUCC@@ is a probability over the algorithm's own coins (the centres and the isolation shifts, charged) for the fixed target, derived from the one score-critical premise H_root (an assumption, no proof) as 1 - (1 - q)^K - K(eps_coin + eps_iso) with q = @@Q@@.

Evidence is separate from the bound: our executed full-scale runs at r = 3, 4, 5@@R6_PHRASE@@ used the fixed centres 1, 2, ... (no coins) and are reported in proof.md section 10 as evidence only. No collision at r = @@R@@ is claimed or shown, and no test reaches the claimed degree.

heuristics.statement: For the fixed polynomial F of proof.md section 2.3 at r = @@R@@ (degree 5^@@DEXP@@), let G_c = gcd(g_c, S^((p-1)/2) - 1) for the odd part g_c about the centre c (proof.md section 3), and let E_c be the event 1 <= deg G_c <= @@DMAX@@ (g_c has between 1 and @@DMAX@@ distinct roots in F_p that are nonzero squares). Then the fraction rho of centres c in F_p with E_c satisfies rho >= q = @@Q@@. For a uniformly random polynomial of degree m the number of its roots in F_p is asymptotically Poisson with mean 1 (a root exists with probability 1 - 1/e = 0.632), each root is a nonzero square with probability one half, so the number of usable roots is Poisson with mean 1/2, giving 1 - exp(-1/2) = 0.3935 minus a negligible tail beyond @@DMAX@@; the premise is that the fixed F behaves this way over uniform centres. The algorithm draws its centres from its own coins, so the events for its K = @@K@@ centres are independent with parameter rho by construction, and P[success] >= 1 - (1 - q)^K - K(eps_coin + eps_iso) = @@P_SUCC_EXACT@@ (proof.md section 9.2).
heuristics.scope: The fixed Poseidon target poseidon-orchard-r@@R@@-prefix-v1, this line construction (the line j = 0 of the first two rounds, the odd part about a centre, proof.md sections 2-3), the event E_c above, centres uniform on F_p. Nothing else in the claim is heuristic apart from the supporting charging rules H1-charging-rules: the isolation lemma (section 9.3), the independence of the centres (from the coins) and the operation counts are proved or counted in proof.md.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the random-polynomial value to the fixed F at degree 5^@@DEXP@@, a degree that no test reaches. Support (not proof): the executed full-scale outcomes at r = 3, 4, 5@@R6_PHRASE@@ (proof.md section 10.1) and a toy measurement at degree 125 and 625 over a 13-bit field (experiment toy-root-fraction); the sensitivity of the bound to a smaller q is in the table of proof.md section 9.2.
heuristics.limitations: An assumption with no proof known to us. Nothing in the algebra forces the fraction of good centres of the fixed F to equal the random-polynomial value; the odd parts g_c for different c all come from one F and are not independent polynomials. The executed outcomes at r = 3 to @@R6_MAX@@ are single deterministic runs with the fixed centres 1, 2, ... that stop at their first success: they are evidence, not a sample, and give no lower bound on rho. The toy experiment uses other functions over another field. The organizer experiment kind infers no probability. No test reaches the claimed degree: one trial at r = @@R@@ needs @@TRIAL_MEM@@ of memory and was not run.

heuristics.statement: The counts of proof.md sections 6 and 7 describe the program of proof.md section 11 under the stated rules: 1 per field operation (a Montgomery conversion is one multiplication), 1 per element load or store plus 1 address operation, 3 per loop iteration plus 2 per loop exit (loops written with the macro FOR8 are unrolled eight times in the source and charged 3 per pass of eight; the generated kernels are straight-line), 1 per other executed index or control operation, @@C@@ per reduced permutation evaluation, @@COIN_WORD_COST@@ per 64-bit coin word, the allocator charged per executed operation, and a register file of 18 words of 256 bits per transform block as the only register assumption. The program runs on one thread; there is no dispatch.
heuristics.scope: All stages of the program of proof.md section 4 at the target dimensions (m = @@M@@, @@N2@@ evaluations of the line and transforms of @@H@@ points), at their worst case over coins and data (proof.md section 6).
heuristics.extrapolation: The worst-case counts are derived from the source by formula (proof.md section 6) and validated against the counters of the executed runs at smaller r (proof.md section 6.1); the r = @@R@@ ledger itself is not a measured run.
heuristics.limitations: The counts are produced by formula from the source, which is part of the proof text and was not run at r = @@R@@ by us or by the organizer. Word-level costs outside the stated rules (cache, bandwidth) are not part of the model.
